title: Equilibrium Matching: Generative Modeling with Implicit Energy-Based Models
claim: Prior methods learn time-varying, non-equilibrium dynamics; ours learns a single time-invariant equilibrium field that converges to the same targets.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right; three time-indexed baseline panels, divider, one ours panel
description: A single row of four 2D vector-field plots. The three left panels, titled Flow Matching at t=0, 0.5 and 1, show black arrows over blue-to-red contour lines. Two blue stars mark the ground-truth targets. The field and contours change with time. At t=0 the contours are concentric rings and the arrows point outward from the centre. At t=0.5 the rings stretch into an elongated loop around both stars. At t=1 the field splits into two basins, one around each star. A thin vertical line separates these from the right panel, titled Equilibrium Matching. That panel shows one static field with two basins whose arrows converge on the same two stars. Blue contours mark low-energy regions and red contours mark high-energy regions. The eye goes first to the stars and the changing contours across the left three panels.
caption: Conceptual 2D Visualization. We compare the conceptual 2D dynamics of Equilibrium Matching and Flow Matching under 2 ground truths (marked by stars). Left: Flow Matching learns non-equilibrium velocity that varies over time. Right: Equilibrium Matching learns an equilibrium gradient that is time-invariant.
abstract: We introduce Equilibrium Matching (EqM), a generative modeling framework built from an equilibrium dynamics perspective. EqM discards the non-equilibrium, time-conditional dynamics in traditional diffusion and flow-based generative models and instead learns the equilibrium gradient of an implicit energy landscape. Through this approach, we can adopt an optimization-based sampling process at inference time, where samples are obtained by gradient descent on the learned landscape with adjustable step sizes, adaptive optimizers, and adaptive compute. Empirically, EqM achieves the best FID among the tested methods, reaching 1.90 on ImageNet 256$\times$256, while remaining competitive on other metrics. Theoretically, we show under standard assumptions that real images are attracting critical points of the learned field and the energy interpretation applies when the field is conservative. Beyond generation, EqM is a flexible framework that naturally handles tasks including partially noised image denoising, OOD detection, and image composition. By replacing time-conditional velocities with a unified equilibrium landscape, EqM offers a tighter bridge between flow and energy-based models and a simple route to optimization-driven inference.
